## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekattharaṇatuvaṭṭana Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 32) is a monastic training rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka governing sleeping arrangements among nuns [SuttaCentral]. The rule formulates that if two nuns lie down together sharing both an under-sheet and an upper covering (*yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvatteyyum, pācittiyan ti*), they commit an offense requiring expiation [Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravāda Vinaya rules for nuns, Ute Hüsken observes that while a corresponding prohibition in the Cullavagga prevents monks from sharing plates, drinking vessels, bedding, or mantles, Pācittiya 32 explicitly targets nuns sharing both a mat or sheet (*attharaṇa*) and a blanket or cloak (*pāvuraṇa*) while lying down together; the casuistic commentary and non-offense (*anāpatti*) formulations indicate that the critical defining element of the offense is lying down together in this manner [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral confirm that this rule is preserved across the disciplinary codes of major early Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral]. Parallels include the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 114) and *Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa*, as well as Chinese translations of the vinayas of the Mahāsaṅghika (Pc 114), Dharmaguptaka (Pc 91), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 149 and 150), and Sarvāstivāda (Pc 88 and 89) traditions, alongside the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 32) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 253 shared passages across 82 Pali texts—most prominently formulaic narrative frames, definitions, and exemption formulas shared with other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules including Pācittiya 42, 87, 85, and Saṅghādisesa 3—as well as an automatic cross-language alignment with the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* [DharmaNexus]. Modern translations include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali and a German translation and commentary by Ute Hüsken [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997].
